definitions: To attribute something, often a failure or negative outcome, to a particular cause or reason.
To consider something as being caused by a specific factor, often to explain it away or accept it.
examples: We lost the game, but we’ll just chalk it up to a lack of practice.
She forgot her lines, but the director decided to chalk it up to first-night nerves.
The project delay was chalked up to unforeseen technical difficulties.
